case_number: Civil Appeal Nos. of 2023 [Arising out of SLP (Civil) Nos. 4302-4303 of 2021 and 5026-5027 of 2021]
summary: The case involves a challenge to the Gujarat High Court's decision upholding the Departmental Selection Committee's post-result reduction of qualifying marks for the post of Supervisor Instructor Class III to accommodate candidates under horizontal reservations (women, ex-servicemen, and persons with disabilities). The reduction, from 60% to 40% for general category and 55% to 35% for reserved categories, was made after the exam and result declaration, effectively converting horizontal reservation into vertical. The appellants, qualified candidates excluded due to the mark reduction, claimed violation of equality and vested rights. The Court examined whether the Selection Committee had the power to alter cut-off marks post-result and whether such action undermined the fairness of recruitment.
legal_provisions_cited: Tej Prakash Pathak & Ors. v. Rajasthan High Court & Ors. (2013) 4 SCC 540
Veerendra Kumar Gautam & Ors. v. Karuna Nidhan Upadhyay & Ors. (2016) 14 SCC 18
Anupal Singh & Ors. v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors. (2020) 2 SCC 173
Ashok Kumar Thakur v. Union of India & Ors. (2008) 6 SCC 1
final_judgment: The Supreme Court allowed the civil appeals, holding that the post-result reduction of cut-off marks by the Selection Committee, especially after the result was published, was impermissible and arbitrary. The action effectively converted horizontal reservation into vertical without amendment to the advertisement, violating the principle of equal opportunity. The decision of the Gujarat High Court's Division Bench upholding the mark reduction was set aside, and the original order of the Single Judge in favor of the appellants was restored.
